context: Two managers handle a customer-service issue
purpose: Teach: 支障/通行/務める/打ち出し/最善/適度/応える/相次い

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: クレームが相次いでいる。業務に支障が出ているよ。
lines.en: Complaints are coming in repeatedly. It's starting to affect operations.
lines.style: Direct, serious. Controlled urgency—not panicked, but clearly concerned. Deliberate pace on the problem statement. Slight tension in the throat.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: はい。担当を務める佐藤、適度な人員増を打ち出したいと。
lines.en: Yes. Sato, who's handling this, wants to propose bringing on some additional staff.
lines.style: Attentive, measured. Reporting facts clearly without editorializing. Slight deference in the tone—supportive but not enthusiastic. Even pacing, steady eye contact.

lines.speaker: yuki_office
lines.jp: 最善策を、明日の会議で決めよう。お客様に応える姿勢、ぶれずに。
lines.en: Let's decide on the best approach at tomorrow's meeting. We need to stay consistent in how we respond to customers.
lines.style: Calm authority. Measured and firm—not barking orders, but drawing a clear line. Lands on 「ぶれずに」 with quiet conviction. Organized, forward-looking.

lines.speaker: kenji_office
lines.jp: 通行止めの案内も、再確認しておきます。
lines.en: I'll double-check the closure announcements as well.
lines.style: Practical, agreeable. Quiet nod in the voice—following through without needing to be asked twice. Slight fadeout at the end, reassuring without fanfare.
